extracted.intended_audience: USPTO patent examiners and patent practitioners (attorneys/agents), applicants
extracted.subtask_description: Form-paragraph guidance for determining when patent claims are distinct/unrelated and for drafting restriction requirements, election/traversal language, rejoinder notices, and double-patenting rejections in U.S. patent examination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Combination-Subcombination distinctness
rubrics_metrics.description: Inventions are related as combination and subcombination and are distinct if (1) the combination as claimed does not require the particulars of the subcombination as claimed for patentability, and (2) the subcombination has utility by itself or in other combinations (MPEP § 806.05(c)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used when claims are presented to both combination(s) and subcombination(s). In bracket 3 specify limitations of the claimed subcombination not required by the claimed combination or evidence supporting that conclusion. In bracket 4 suggest a utility for the subcombination other than its use in the combination. Conclude with form paragraph 8.21. If applicant elects a subcombination and claims thereto are later allowable, dependent claims requiring all limitations of the allowable subcombination will be examined per 37 CFR 1.104; applicant may face provisional statutory/nonstatutory double patenting issues in continuations/divisionals. See MPEP § 806.05(c).

rubrics_metrics.name: Subcombinations usable together distinctness
rubrics_metrics.description: Subcombinations disclosed as usable together in a single combination are distinct if they do not overlap in scope, are not obvious variants, and at least one subcombination is separately usable (MPEP § 806.05(d)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use when claims are presented to subcombinations usable together. In bracket 3 identify the subcombination (group number or identifier); in bracket 4 suggest a separate utility other than use with the other subcombination. Conclude with form paragraph 8.21. If applicant elects and claims to the elected subcombination become allowable, dependent claims requiring all limitations will be examined per 37 CFR 1.104.

rubrics_metrics.name: Process and apparatus distinctness
rubrics_metrics.description: Process and apparatus claims are distinct if either: (1) the process as claimed can be practiced by another materially different apparatus or by hand, or (2) the apparatus as claimed can be used to practice another materially different process (MPEP § 806.05(e)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this paragraph when claims are presented to both a process and apparatus for its practice. In bracket 3 explain which condition applies. Follow with paragraph 8.21.04 to notify applicant of potential rejoinder of process claims if product/apparatus claims are later allowed. If a product claim is allowable, process claims depending from or requiring all limitations of the product may be rejoined (see 37 CFR 1.104).

rubrics_metrics.name: Apparatus and product-made distinctness
rubrics_metrics.description: Apparatus and product-made inventions are distinct if either: (1) the apparatus as claimed is not an obvious apparatus for making the product and the apparatus can be used to make a materially different product, or (2) the product as claimed can be made by another materially different apparatus (MPEP § 806.05(g)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In bracket 3 insert one or more supporting reasons (e.g., apparatus can be used to make a different product, product can be made by a materially different apparatus, or process can be practiced by hand). A process is 'by hand' if performable without any apparatus. Conclude the restriction requirement with form paragraph 8.21. Follow with form paragraph 8.21.04 to notify of potential rejoinder of process claims. See MPEP § 806.05(g).

rubrics_metrics.name: Product and process-of-making distinctness
rubrics_metrics.description: Product and process-of-making the product are distinct if either: (1) the process as claimed can be used to make another materially different product, or (2) the product as claimed can be made by another materially different process (MPEP § 806.05(f)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use when claims are presented to both a product and the process of making the product. In bracket 3 state the applicable reason(s) (e.g., process makes a materially different product, product made by materially different process). Conclude with form paragraph 8.21. Follow rejoinder practice (8.21.04) for rejoining process claims if appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Product and process-of-using distinctness
rubrics_metrics.description: Product and process-of-using the product can be shown distinct if either: (1) the process for using the product can be practiced with another materially different product, or (2) the product as claimed can be used in a materially different process of using that product (MPEP § 806.05(h)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use when claims are presented to both the product and a process of using the product. If process-of-making claims that are specially adapted for making the product are present, those should be grouped with the product invention (MPEP § 806.05(i)). In bracket 3 insert specific reasons (examples provided). Conclude with form paragraph 8.21 and, where applicable, follow with 8.21.04 for rejoinder notice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unrelated inventions criterion
rubrics_metrics.description: Inventions are unrelated if they are not disclosed as capable of use together and they have different designs, modes of operation, and effects (MPEP § 802.01 and § 806.06).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use only when claims are presented to truly unrelated inventions (example: a necktie and a locomotive bearing). In bracket 3 insert reasons for concluding inventions are unrelated. This form paragraph must be followed by form paragraph 8.21.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unrelated product and process inventions criterion
rubrics_metrics.description: Product and process inventions are unrelated if it can be shown that the product cannot be used in, or made by, the process (MPEP § 802.01 and § 806.06).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In bracket 3 insert reasons for concluding product and process are unrelated. This form paragraph must be followed by form paragraph 8.21.

rubrics_metrics.name: Burden and requirement for election / traversal
rubrics_metrics.description: Restriction is proper because the listed inventions are independent or distinct and there would be a serious search and/or examination burden if restriction were not required; the reply must include (i) an election of an invention to be examined even if traversed and (ii) identification of the claims encompassing the elected invention (37 CFR 1.143).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In bracket 1 insert the specific reason(s) why a search/examination burden exists (examples: separate classification; recognized divergent subject matter; different field of search such as different classes/subclasses, electronic resources, or search strategies). Election may be made with or without traverse; to reserve petition rights, election must be with traverse. A traverse must distinctly and specifically point out alleged errors to be timely; failure to timely traverse results in loss of petition right under 37 CFR 1.144. If claims are added after election, applicant must indicate which are readable on the elected invention. If applicant traverses on ground that inventions are not patentably distinct, applicant should submit evidence or identify such evidence now, or clearly admit they are obvious variants; examiner may use evidence/admission in a 35 U.S.C. 103 rejection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice of potential rejoinder of process claims
rubrics_metrics.description: When restriction is between product/apparatus and process claims, withdrawn process claims that include all limitations of an allowable product/apparatus claim should be considered for rejoinder; rejoined claims will be fully examined per 37 CFR 1.104.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To be rejoined, withdrawn process claims must include all limitations of the allowable product/apparatus claim; rejoined claims must meet 35 U.S.C. 101, 102, 103 and 112. Withdrawn process claims not commensurate in scope with an allowable product/apparatus claim will not be rejoined. Applicant is advised to amend process claims during prosecution to require limitations of product/apparatus claims; failure to do so may prevent rejoinder. Note that 35 U.S.C. 121 double-patenting prohibition does not apply where restriction is withdrawn before issue. Use form paragraph 8.21.04 at the end of relevant restriction requirements (process vs product/apparatus/making/using). See MPEP § 821.04 for rejoinder practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Answer to arguments with traverse (finalizing restriction)
rubrics_metrics.description: If applicant elects with traverse and traversal is noted on specified grounds, the examiner may find the traversal unpersuasive for specified reasons and make the restriction requirement final.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use form paragraph 8.25 to acknowledge the election with traverse, state the traversal ground(s), explain why the traversal is not persuasive, and indicate the requirement remains proper and is made FINAL.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement when elected by telephone
rubrics_metrics.description: If a provisional election was made during a telephone conversation, the election must be affirmed by applicant in reply; withdrawn claims are identified and confirmation provided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In bracket 1 insert the invention elected; in bracket 3 summarize ground(s) for traverse if any; in bracket 4 insert reasons why traversal not persuasive. Use when a telephone election was made and must be followed up in writing. Claim withdrawn from further consideration under 37 CFR 1.142(b) if drawn to a non-elected invention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Election without traverse (acknowledgement and follow-up)
rubrics_metrics.description: The applicant's election without traverse is acknowledged; an action on the merits of claims to the elected invention should follow.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In bracket 3 insert 'with' or 'without' as applicable; in bracket 4 insert elected group or species. Use form paragraph 8.25.01 when election is without traverse.

rubrics_metrics.name: No election by telephone (documentation of attempted call)
rubrics_metrics.description: When a telephone call was made to request an oral election but no election was made, note the attempted contact and require written reply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In bracket 1 insert name of person contacted and in bracket 2 insert date(s) of contact. Use when a telephone election was attempted but applicant's representative did not or would not make an election. Do not use if no contact was made.

rubrics_metrics.name: Joint inventors — correction of inventorship upon cancellation
rubrics_metrics.description: If claims to a non-elected invention are canceled, inventorship must be corrected under 37 CFR 1.48(a) if any currently named inventor is no longer an inventor of at least one remaining claim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A request to correct inventorship under 37 CFR 1.48(a) must be accompanied by an application data sheet per 37 CFR 1.76 identifying each inventor by legal name and the processing fee under 37 CFR 1.17(i). Use form paragraph 8.23.02 where applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Election treated as without traverse due to incomplete reply
rubrics_metrics.description: If applicant's reply does not distinctly and specifically point out supposed errors in the restriction requirement, the election is treated as an election without traverse (MPEP § 818.01(a)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Acknowledge the election and note the reply date. Use form paragraph 8.25.02. This situation results from incomplete or non-specific traversal arguments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Canceled elected claims — non-responsive amendment
rubrics_metrics.description: An amendment cancelling all claims drawn to the elected invention and presenting only claims to a non-elected invention is non-responsive (MPEP § 821.03); remaining claims are not readable on the elected invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State why remaining claims are not readable on the elected invention in bracket 2. Applicant is given a TIME PERIOD of TWO MONTHS from mailing date to supply omission/correction to avoid abandonment; extensions under 37 CFR 1.136(a) are available. Do not use for applications granted special status under accelerated examination — use 8.26.AE instead.

rubrics_metrics.name: Canceled elected claims non-responsive — accelerated examination variant
rubrics_metrics.description: Same as 8.26 but for applications under the accelerated examination program (filed on/after Aug 25, 2006) or other special status under 37 CFR 1.102(c)(2) or (d).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant is given TWO (2) MONTHS to correct; extensions under 37 CFR 1.136(a) are available but filing a petition for extension will remove application from the accelerated program. Replies must be filed electronically via EFS-Web to meet the 12-month objective; non-electronic replies may delay final disposition beyond 12 months.

rubrics_metrics.name: Different inventors, common assignee, same invention — AIA (FITF) handling
rubrics_metrics.description: If a claim is directed to the same invention as a claim of a commonly assigned patent/application, more than one patent may not be issued on the same invention; applicant should amend or cancel claims so applications do not contain claims directed to the same invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include form paragraph 7.03.aia when using this paragraph. In bracket 3 insert the U.S. patent or copending application number. Do not use this paragraph if one invention would have been obvious in view of the other (use 8.28.aia instead). Also advise on provisional/actual double patenting rejections (8.31/8.32) and possible 35 U.S.C. 102(a)(2) rejections (7.15.01.aia/7.15.02.aia) if earlier effective filing date applies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Different inventors, common assignee, same invention — pre-AIA (FTI) handling
rubrics_metrics.description: If a claim is directed to the same invention as that of a commonly assigned patent/application under pre-AIA (first to invent) law, priority issues under pre-AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(f)/(g) must be resolved.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The applicant must amend/cancel claims or the assignee must identify the prior inventor. The USPTO normally will not institute an interference between commonly owned applications/patents. A terminal disclaimer has no effect in this situation because the issue is priority, not extension of monopoly. Failure to comply may result in abandonment. Use form paragraph 7.03.fti and appropriate 7.15/7.19 paragraphs where applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inventions not patentably distinct — AIA (advice & procedures)
rubrics_metrics.description: If an application is commonly assigned with a patent/application that includes claims patentably indistinct from those in the present application, and common ownership as of the effective filing date has not been established, the claims are considered not patentably distinct.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use form paragraph 8.28.aia. Follow with 8.28.01.aia which advises applicant that they may submit a statement under 35 U.S.C. 102(b)(2)(C) / 37 CFR 1.104(c)(4)(i) to show common ownership as of the effective filing date, or a 35 U.S.C. 102(c) / 37 CFR 1.104(c)(4)(ii) statement showing joint research agreement facts and parties, and amend application to disclose names of parties. If common ownership is shown, rejections under 35 U.S.C. 102/103 based on the commonly assigned case will be precluded. Alternatively applicant may amend/cancel claims so claims are not patentably indistinct. A nonstatutory double patenting rejection should also be included (form paragraphs 8.34–8.37).

rubrics_metrics.name: Inventions not patentably distinct — pre-AIA advisory & procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: For pre-AIA (first to invent) cases where commonly assigned claims are patentably indistinct but common ownership at time of invention isn't established, the applicant must resolve priority or amend/cancel claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use form paragraph 8.28.fti and follow with 8.28.01.fti. May require naming the prior inventor under pre-AIA 35 U.S.C. 103(c) and 37 CFR 1.78(g) or amending/canceling claims. Include appropriate 7.21.fti / 7.21.01.fti / 7.21.02.fti rejections as needed; include nonstatutory double patenting paragraphs 8.34–8.37 as applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advisory about commonly assigned prior art and remedies
rubrics_metrics.description: If a commonly assigned case would be prior art under 35 U.S.C. 102(a)(2) because common ownership as of effective filing date is not shown, applicant can file statements under 35 U.S.C. 102(b)(2)(C)/102(c) or amend/cancel claims to avoid rejections under 35 U.S.C. 102/103.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains how showing common ownership or joinder under joint research agreement will preclude certain rejections; if not shown, applicant must amend/cancel claims. This advisory should follow form paragraph 8.28 and is used only once in an Office action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patentably indistinct claims in copending applications
rubrics_metrics.description: When claim(s) of this application are patentably indistinct from claim(s) in a copending application, elimination from all but one application may be required absent good and sufficient reason (37 CFR 1.78(f)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant is required to cancel patentably indistinct claims from all but one application or maintain a clear line of demarcation between applications. See MPEP § 822. Use form paragraph 8.29 and insert reference application number where indicated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory double patenting — 35 U.S.C. 101 (same-invention) heading and remedy
rubrics_metrics.description: A statutory double patenting rejection (same invention type) is founded on the principle that one inventor may obtain a patent for a single invention only (35 U.S.C. 101); 'same invention' means identical subject matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This heading (form paragraph 8.30) must precede statutory-type double patenting rejections (8.31/8.32). A statutory double patenting rejection can be overcome by canceling or amending claims so they are no longer coextensive in scope. Filing of a terminal disclaimer cannot overcome a 35 U.S.C. 101 double patenting rejection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rejection — 35 U.S.C. 101 double patenting (statutory)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use when claim(s) are rejected under 35 U.S.C. 101 as claiming the same invention as claim(s) of a prior U.S. patent (statutory double patenting).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Must be preceded by form paragraph 8.30. Insert references and bracketed items per instructions. For pre-AIA and AIA contexts include additional form paragraphs as appropriate (e.g., 8.27.fti/8.27.aia, 7.15.* paragraphs) and consider evidence that a patent is prior art under pre-AIA sections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provisional rejection — 35 U.S.C. 101 double patenting (copending application)
rubrics_metrics.description: Claim(s) are provisionally rejected under 35 U.S.C. 101 as claiming the same invention as claim(s) of a copending application (provisional statutory double patenting since the claims have not been patented).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Must be preceded by form paragraph 8.30. Use only for copending application references (not issued patents). Insert reference application number in bracket 3. A provisional rejection in the reference application should also be made. For pre-AIA and AIA cases, include related form paragraphs (8.28.fti/8.28.aia and 7.15.fti etc.) as applicable.
